review_items.review_title: Fulfilled expectations: A critical evaluation of NIT Arunachal Pradesh

aspect_evidence.evidence_summary: 'As of now, around 40% of the students got placed in my batch. Among those, the highest package is 9 LPA, the lowest is 4.5 LPA and the average package is 6 LPA. The top recruiter is L&T. Placement drives are still going on, and we expect better ones in the second half. In our senior batch, almost each student got 2-3 jobs.'
'There are two college fests, Addovedi the technical fest and Atulyam the cultural fest. As the campus has recently shifted, these fests don't meet most of the students' expectations.'

'The major drawback of this college is connectivity. If you need to buy anything, most of the time you need to go to Itanagar. There are only two buses to Itanagar, and the timings are bad. There are no buses in college. So while going to classes, you will be walking down the hill. On Sunday, there is no transport. As of now, we can say that connectivity is the worst.'

'The infrastructure of academic buildings is not bad. But you will be disappointed if you place high hopes on infrastructure. In hostels, we get almost all the facilities. The only things that concern us are power cuts and connectivity. Only BSNL works there, so to use the internet, we need to depend solely on Wi-Fi.'

review_items.extraction_note: This is a genuinely notable, specific, and verifiable-sounding claim: a recurring seasonal water shortage severe enough to require revision of the academic calendar, distinct from generic infrastructure complaints.

aspect_evidence.evidence_summary: 'High-quality bed facilities, great hostel, every room have its own balcony and you will get fresh air and beautiful greenery of mountains. All students were very happy in this college; very good facilities compared to other colleges.'
'Library facilities are available but very poor and also transportation facilities in college is very poor.'
'During winter season, there is acute shortage of water in campus and students suffer from this situation every year, due to which academic calendar is revised sometimes.'
'Infrastructure is very bad, you will struggle for basic needs like electricity, water, food, because it is a new campus and everything is starting from scratch.'
'The cultural activities here are the best; you can celebrate many festivals including [the] Arunachal local fest.'
'The placement of the college is just okay. In comparison to many other NITs, the placement is just average.'

'Faculty-student ratio in NIT Arunachal Pradesh is good, it is almost 20 teachers per 100 students. Most teachers are Ph.D. holders and [have] minimum 10-year experience. And for lab work facility [there] is a Ph.D. student. Exam levels are moderate.'

'The placement of the college is good. The placement and training committee plays a very important role during the placement round... The college has a record of 100% placement... The highest package for our batch was around 18 LPA and the average package was approx 7.2 LPA.' (Note: this positive claim appears in the same aggregated snippet block as the more neutral 'just okay' assessment above, suggesting these may be two distinct reviewers concatenated on the same page rather than one contradictory account.)

review_items.extraction_note: This item is a secondhand account (a cousin's relayed experience), and the surrounding page text appears to be partly an editorial/summary description rather than purely a direct student review; content_type marked 'other' to reflect this mixed nature.

aspect_evidence.evidence_summary: 'Overall, NIT Arunachal Pradesh offers satisfactory campus life. Hostel facilities are decent. The campus has two hostels for girls. Rooms are spacious. The hostel has 24 hours Wi-Fi and LAN facilities. The mess food won't be satisfactory in terms of taste but it is hygienic and clean.' Separately: 'It all depends upon which hostel is assigned to you. If you are lucky you might get to live with 2-3 students or you will [live] with at least 7 students in a single room.'

review_items.extraction_note: IMPORTANT DATA QUALITY FLAG: This page states 'There are 10 hostels, 2 for girls and 8 for boys,' while a different page from the same GetMyUni source (facilities page, retrieved earlier) states 'There are 7 halls of residence in total, five for boys and two for girls.' These two figures from the same platform are directly inconsistent with each other; both are preserved as separate observations rather than reconciled, since resolving genuine source inconsistency is a backend decision, not an extraction-layer one.

aspect_evidence.evidence_summary: 'Fooding quality is not so good. The hostel is run by the hostel mess in-charge who made a contract with the college and runs the mess. Hostel fee is free but mess fee is not. Mess fee is around Rs 3500 per month.'

'Classroom quality is also not up to the mark as compared to other NITs. There are no separate buildings for each department. The college campus is not permanent. The permanent site is under construction.'
'There is no students' society but students gather if there is a mass need.'

review_items.review_title: Improving with limited amount of resources
review_items.extraction_note: Batch of 2025. Sub-ratings: Placements 4, Infrastructure 4, Faculty & Course Curriculum 5, Crowd & Campus Life 5, Value for Money 4.

aspect_evidence.evidence_summary: 'Infrastructure related to studies is good but medical facilities and sports curriculum still need improvement. There is improvement of canteen facilities and mess food quality but it still requires more [work]. The construction of [the] central library is ongoing and it has one library that is functional.'
'Wi-Fi is being provided in a hostel and the campus. The central library is still under construction. The infrastructure of the college is not much good. It's still under construction.'
'The food served in the mess is good.'
'Medical facilities are not good.'

'NIT Arunachal Pradesh does not have a ragging culture. The institute has strict restrictions and policies for ragging, and also has an Anti-Ragging Squad. At the time of admission, students have to sign the affidavit regarding the ragging [policy].'
